article_title: History of the New England Patriots

msg.content:
<document>
<title>History of the New England Patriots</title>
<fragment>
![](image)Head coach Bill Belichick transformed the Patriots into a perennial Super Bowl contender.

</fragment>
<fragment>

The Patriots faced the Steelers in the AFC Championship Game.[264] After Brady injured his ankle in the second quarter, Bledsoe came off the sideline and led the team to their only offensive touchdown of the game.[264][265] In the second half, with two special teams touchdowns and two fourth-quarter interceptions of passes thrown by Pittsburgh's Kordell Stewart, the Patriots upset the Steelers 24–17 to advance to Super Bowl XXXVI.[265][266]



![](image)Quarterback Tom Brady led the Patriots to six Super Bowl wins and nine Super Bowl appearances.
In the Super Bowl, the Patriots faced the St. Louis Rams, led by league MVP Kurt Warner.[267] During the game, Bill Belichick used a defensive game plan that used the blitz sparingly, but chipped the Rams receivers and running back Marshall Faulk as they went into their patterns.[268] This plan forced three turnovers.[269]


</fragment>
<fragment>
![](image)President George W. Bush poses with the New England Patriots during a ceremony honoring the Super Bowl XXXIX champions in the Rose Garden.
With a 14–2 record and the second seed in the AFC playoffs,[305] the Patriots defeated the Colts at home in the playoffs.[306] The Patriots then defeated the top-seeded Steelers on the road, 41–27, in the AFC Championship Game.[307] The Patriots' defeated the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl XXXIX 24–21 in their second straight Super Bowl victory.[308] As of 2021[update], the 2003–2004 New England Patriots are the most recent team to win back-to-back Super Bowls.[309]



### 2005–06: Playoff losses

[edit]

Main articles: 2005 New England Patriots season and 2006 New England Patriots season


</fragment>
<fragment>

After beating the Tennessee Titans in the divisional round,[449] the Patriots faced the Jacksonville Jaguars.[450] In the fourth quarter, Brady led the team back from a ten-point deficit to take the lead, 24–20.[450] The Patriots won and earned a trip to their eighth Super Bowl.[450] In Super Bowl LII, Brady set a Super Bowl record with 505 yards passing.[451] Brady tried to lead a comeback to win the game in the fourth quarter, but defensive end Brandon Graham strip-sacked Brady, and the ball was recovered by the Eagles.[451][452] This, along with a failed last-second Hail Mary pass, resulted in the Patriots losing 41–33.[453]



### 2018: Sixth Super Bowl Championship

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
In 2014, the Patriots finished 12–4 and won their sixth straight AFC East title.[410] They were the top seed, had a first round bye and had home field advantage for the AFC playoffs.[410]


The Patriots defeated the Baltimore Ravens 35–31 in the divisional round of the playoffs.[411] They then defeated the Indianapolis Colts 45–7 to advance to Super Bowl XLIX against the defending Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks.[412] After a scoreless first quarter, both teams exchanged two touchdowns to make it 14–14 at halftime.[413] Seattle then scored a field goal and a touchdown to take a 10-point lead going into the final quarter.[413] The Patriots rallied, scoring two touchdowns to take a 28–24 lead with 2:02 remaining.[413] After the Seahawks drove all the way to the 1 yard line with under a minute to go, rookie cornerback Malcolm Butler caught an interception on Seattle's final offensive play, winning the game for the Patriots.[413] Brady won his third Super Bowl MVP award.[414]




</fragment>
</document>

The Patriots have won six Super Bowl championships (XXXVI, XXXVIII, XXXIX, XLIX, LI, and LIII). They also played in and lost Super Bowls XX, XXXI, XLII, XLVI, and LII. During the 2007 regular season, the Patriots became the only NFL team in history to win 16 games, and the first since the 1972 Miami Dolphins (in a 14-game season) to complete the regular campaign undefeated.[8] Belichick's Patriots are one of only two teams to win three Super Bowls in four years (the other being the Dallas Cowboys from 1993 to 1996).[9]


</fragment>
<fragment>

Since Bill Belichick was hired as the team's head coach in 2000, the Patriots have won six Super Bowls, nine AFC Championship Games, and sixteen AFC East titles, while amassing a regular season record of 237–82.[4] The team's quarterback over that same period, Tom Brady, was awarded the NFL Most Valuable Player (MVP)[5][6] three times, and the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player four times (he later won another Super Bowl MVP with the Buccaneers); he is one of only five players named Super Bowl MVP more than once, and the only one named more than three times.[7]
